title: Perfect Investigation
verdict: Every lie answered, down to the paint on his hand.
narrative: You lay it out for {accused} in the house manager's office: the box door, the pass-door key, the gilt still tacky on the candlestick, the letter from Hollywood. He doesn't wait for the last one.
He confesses before the Sunday papers go to press. Eighteen years, he says, and a carbon copy. The insurance would have lapsed on Monday.
The Orpheum dims its lights for a week. Felix Marsh opens as Edmund in September, to the best notices of the year.

title: True Criminal
verdict: The right name, and enough to hold it.
narrative: {accused} is charged on Sunday morning, still insisting he wept in the last act.
The case holds, though his counsel makes much of the questions you never asked and the statements you never broke.
He is convicted in the autumn. The Orpheum never puts on The Glass Widow again.

title: Wrong Suspect
verdict: A careful case, built around the wrong person.
narrative: Your case against {accused} is careful. It has a motive, a lie, and a timeline. It is also wrong.
The charges collapse at the committal hearing. By then, someone has cleared out an office and burned a great deal of paper.
The file is reopened in the winter and handed to somebody else.

title: Innocent Person Accused
verdict: An arrest on a hunch, in front of the whole company.
narrative: {accused} is taken out through the stage door in handcuffs while the press photographers wait on Canal Street.
The charges are dropped within the week. The photographs aren't.
Julian Crane's killer is never named. The Orpheum's ghost stories get a new chapter.

title: Criminal Escapes
verdict: The curtain came down, and nobody was holding the rope.
narrative: The Sunday papers go to press with 'MYSTERY AT THE ORPHEUM' and no name beneath it.
Whoever walked into Dressing Room 1 walked out again, and has kept walking.
Case #048 is filed under Unsolved. The candlestick is returned to the props table, polished.
